Use one of the recommended methods below. For more installation options, uninstall steps, and troubleshooting, see the [setup documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup). 1. Install Claude Code: **MacOS/Linux (Recommended):** ```bash curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ``` **Homebrew (MacOS/Linux):** ```bash brew install --cask claude-code ``` **Windows (Recommended):** ```powershell irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` **WinGet (Windows):** ```powershell winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode ``` **NPM (Deprecated):** ```bash npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code ``` 2. Navigate to your project directory and run `claude`. ## Plugins This repository includes several Claude Code plugins that extend functionality with custom commands and agents. See the [plugins directory](./plugins/README.md) for detailed documentation on available plugins. ## Reporting Bugs We welcome your feedback. Use the `/bug` command to report issues directly within Claude Code, or file a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues). ## Connect on Discord Join the [Claude Developers Discord](https://anthropic.com/discord) to connect with other developers using Claude Code. Get help, share feedback, and discuss your projects with the community. ## Data collection, usage, and retention When you use Claude Code, we collect feedback, which includes usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the `/bug` command. ### How we use your data See our [data usage policies](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage). ### Privacy safeguards We have implemented several safeguards to protect your data, including limited retention periods for sensitive information, restricted access to user session data, and clear policies against using feedback for model training. readmeHtml:
Claude Code

Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, and handling git workflows -- all through natural language commands. Use it in your terminal, IDE, or tag @claude on Github.

Learn more in the official documentation.

Get started

Note

Installation via npm is deprecated. Use one of the recommended methods below.

For more installation options, uninstall steps, and troubleshooting, see the setup documentation.

  1. Install Claude Code:

    MacOS/Linux (Recommended):

    curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

    Homebrew (MacOS/Linux):

    brew install --cask claude-code

    Windows (Recommended):

    irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

    WinGet (Windows):

    winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode

    NPM (Deprecated):

    npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

  2. Navigate to your project directory and run claude.

Plugins

This repository includes several Claude Code plugins that extend functionality with custom commands and agents. See the plugins directory for detailed documentation on available plugins.

Reporting Bugs

We welcome your feedback. Use the /bug command to report issues directly within Claude Code, or file a GitHub issue.

Connect on Discord

Join the Claude Developers Discord to connect with other developers using Claude Code. Get help, share feedback, and discuss your projects with the community.

Data collection, usage, and retention

When you use Claude Code, we collect feedback, which includes usage data (such as code acceptance or rejections), associated conversation data, and user feedback submitted via the /bug command.

How we use your data

See our data usage policies.

Privacy safeguards

We have implemented several safeguards to protect your data, including limited retention periods for sensitive information, restricted access to user session data, and clear policies against using feedback for model training.

For full details, please review our Commercial Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

releases.name: v2.1.306
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Fixed `claude -p` inside cloud sessions reporting "Not logged in" when started without the session's environment variables
- Fixed an API error being replaced by "prompt is too long", and an unneeded compaction, in sessions with many MCP tools

releases.name: v2.1.305
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added `sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces` so sandboxed commands on Linux can create user namespaces (Chromium, rootless podman); this lets them get around the sandbox's file protections
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG_USAGE_LIMIT_RECHECK_MS` so unattended retry mode (`CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG`) notices a usage limit that was lifted before its reset
- Fixed every request failing on Vertex, Bedrock and other providers when the endpoint or a gateway rejects tool search, and behind gateways with ToolSearch disallowed or left out of `--tools` (a 2.1.304 regression): Claude Code now retries without it
- Fixed `/effort` and `/autocompact` settings not applying when the model name differed from a `modelOverrides` value by letter case or a `[1m]` tag
- Fixed new worktrees in a bare repository sometimes starting from local HEAD instead of the default branch, and unchanged subagent worktrees sometimes not being cleaned up
- Fixed Bash commands on a full disk failing with a raw `ENOSPC` file path: the error now says the disk is full and that nothing ran
- Fixed an MCP server passed by a cloud session or by the SDK's `setMcpServers` being replaced later in the session

releases.name: v2.1.304
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added a transcript line when a plugin that runs first skips one of your mod's hooks, naming the event and the plugin
- Added `decider: "person"` to a mod's `tool.check` answer: only the permission dialog or a host's callback can approve the ask, and it is refused with the mod's reason where nobody can be asked
- Added `e.isReadOnly` to a mod's `tool.check` event, set when the tool call is read-only
- Added `/auto-mode-setup`: a guided setup that reads your project and recent sessions to teach auto mode about your environment, now also available on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, Claude apps gateway and telemetry-disabled sessions
- Added `/claude-api managed-agents-secure`, which compares a Managed Agents agent's settings with Anthropic's published security guide, without changing anything
- Added the names of the tools called earlier to the compaction summary in the transcript view (Ctrl+O)
- Added a warning on Pro and Max plans when resuming an inactive conversation would use a noticeable share of your 5-hour usage limit: resume anyway, or start a new conversation and Claude can look up the previous one if you refer to it
- Fixed the organization policy not refresh

releases.name: v2.1.303
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Bug fixes and reliability improvements

releases.name: v2.1.302
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL` to choose the model the client-side auto mode classifier uses; it does not change the model for server-side auto mode
- Added an `Idle compaction` row to `/config` for turning idle compaction off or back on; the notices shown after an idle compaction now say how to turn it off
- Added a notice to `/design-sync` and `/design-login` that standalone Claude Design (claude.ai/design) closes by December 14, 2026
- Fixed a "Prompt is too long" error when stopping a turn while the conversation was being compacted
- Fixed requests failing with "diagnostics: Extra inputs are not permitted" after switching to Vertex or Bedrock mid-session
- Fixed the Read tool loading an image file of any size, or a pipe or device named like an image, entirely into memory; image sources over 128 MB are now refused
- Fixed `/autocompact` and `/effort` saving to the wrong model when a gateway names Opus 4 or 4.1 with a prefix, such as `anthropic/claude-opus-4-1`
- Fixed a prompt cache miss when a tool added mid-session was loaded again through ToolSearch or after compaction
- Fixed `claude plugin` and other subcommands sometimes exiting before a queued se

aiSummary.oneLiner: An official, terminal-based AI coding assistant powered directly by the Claude model family.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Claude Code is a command-line interface tool developed by Anthropic that deeply integrates their Claude AI models directly into a developer's local environment. It is designed to understand entire codebases by autonomously navigating directories, reading files, and executing local shell commands for context. The tool assists with complex refactoring, bug hunting, and feature implementation without requiring developers to leave their terminal or copy-paste code into a browser. It maintains a secure, local execution perimeter while leveraging the advanced reasoning capabilities of models like Claude 3.5 Sonnet. This drastically reduces context switching and accelerates the software development lifecycle.
keyFeatures: Native terminal integration: Operates entirely within the command line, integrating seamlessly into existing shell environments and workflows.
Autonomous codebase navigation: Capable of searching directories, reading files, and grepping for specific patterns to build context automatically.
Local command execution: Safely runs local tests, linters, and build scripts to verify code changes before finalizing them.
Advanced model reasoning: Powered directly by Anthropic's most capable models, ensuring high-quality architectural advice and code generation.
Context-aware refactoring: Understands the broader repository structure, allowing it to safely execute multi-file changes and updates.

useCases.title: Automated Bug Resolution
useCases.description: Instruct the assistant to locate the source of a specific error trace, write the fix, and run the test suite to verify it.

useCases.title: Complex Code Refactoring
useCases.description: Command the tool to migrate an entire directory of components to a new framework API across multiple interdependent files.

useCases.title: Codebase Onboarding
useCases.description: Ask the terminal assistant to explain the architecture and data flow of a massive, unfamiliar repository dynamically.

useCases.title: Rapid Feature Implementation
useCases.description: Describe a new feature in natural language and allow the tool to scaffold the necessary files, logic, and tests automatically.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Professional software engineers and developers who prefer working in terminal environments and want powerful, context-aware AI assistance. It requires familiarity with command-line interfaces and local development workflows.
